items.s: Brown caught his only target for 52 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime win versus the Browns. He also lost a fumble on a punt return. Brown showed off his plus speed in the second quarter, blowing by safety Ronnie Hickman and coming down with a 52-yard bomb from quarterback Tyler Shough. One series later, though, he coughed up the football during an erratic punt return. Barring an injury to one of the wideouts ahead of him on New Orleans' depth chart, there likely won't be much room in the short term for him to earn a significant role outside of special teams.

items.h: Barion Brown makes splash play in win over Browns
items.s: Barion Brown caught his only target for a big 52-yard gain in the Saints' 23-22 win against the Browns on Sunday. He also returned three kicks for 78 yards and five punts for 68 yards. Brown is making a name for himself on special teams, but is also having success as a deep threat as well. He's not startable in regular leagues, but for those who award return yards, he's been a nice addition.

Brown hauled in all three targets for 57 yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers. Brown had the most productive game of his NFL career thus far, catching more passes than he had in his previous five appearances combined. The 2026 No. 190 overall pick should continue to get consistent work on special teams. However, despite the recent uptick in offensive snaps, it's unknown if Brown will continue to be more involved as a pass-catcher moving forward.

items.h: Barion Brown grabs three passes in loss
items.s: Barion Brown caught all three of his targets for 57 yards in the Saints' 16-10 loss to the Steelers on Sunday. Brown was tied for the Saints' lead in receiving yards with Alvin Kamara, doing it on four fewer receptions, granted Kamara is a running back. Brown just had his first catch last week after proving himself on special teams, so he might have earned himself a larger role moving forward on offense after the Saints' bye week.

Brown (thigh) is active for Sunday's game against the Vikings. Brown was a full participant in Friday's practice, signaling that the returner and No. 4 wide receiver has recovered from the thigh injury he suffered in the Saints' Week 4 loss to the Falcons. Brown is all set to suit up for the Saints and will likely handle most of the return duties in Sunday's contest.

Brown (thigh) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Emily Leiker of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports. Brown was limited by a thigh injury in each of the first two practices of Week 5 prep. Although he's tagged as questionable, his ability to practice in full Friday gives Brown a solid chance at being cleared to play against Minnesota. If the rookie sixth-rounder is ruled out, then Kendre Miller and Jayden Price would likely operate as the Saints' top return options on kickoffs and punts.

Brown recorded one carry for a loss of five yards while also adding 130 kickoff-return yards and a two-yard punt return during Monday night's 45-24 loss to the Falcons. Brown made his return to action Monday after missing the team's Week 3 loss to Las Vegas while nursing a hamstring injury. The wide receiver logged just three snaps on offense, failing to garner a target against Atlanta. Brown will continue to have no offensive upside barring an injury to another member of the Saints' WR room.

Brown (hamstring) has no injury designation ahead of Monday's Week 4 matchup against Atlanta. Brown missed last Sunday's loss to Las Vegas due to a hamstring injury. However, he logged an LP/LP/FP practice progression this week and has been cleared to suit up Monday. Brown's primary role for the Saints this season has been as a kick and punt returner, and he has no targets on offense so far while logging nine offensive snaps through two games.

Brown (hamstring) is listed as out for Sunday's game versus Las Vegas. Brown didn't practice all week due to a hamstring injury and will now miss the first game of his career. The rookie logged a combined nine offensive snaps in Weeks 1 and 2, though his absence will be felt on special teams. As a result, Jayden Price may be busier than usual in Week 3. That could also apply to Kendre Miller (illness), assuming he's not a healthy scratch for the second consecutive game.

items.h: Barrion Brown sees one touch in Week 1
items.s: Barrion Brown rushed once for three yards in the Saints' 31-30 loss to the Detroit Lions in Week 1. Brown was more of an afterthought in the New Orleans offense for head coach Kellen Moore, finishing tied for last in touches in the loss. The wideout can remain off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 2 contest against the Baltimore Ravens.

items.h: Brown rushed twice for 19 yards and a touchdown while adding a four-yard punt return in Friday's 27-24 preseason win over the Cowboys.
items.s: Brown wasn't targeted in the preseason finale but still left his mark on the game with a seven-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter. The rookie sixth-round pick out of LSU reportedly stood out in training camp, and he has built on that success with a strong preseason. Rookie first-round pick Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is expected to miss about two months, so the door is open for Brown to take on a sizable role out of the gate behind Chris Olave in a Saints WR room that also includes Devaughn Vele and Bryce Lance.

items.h: Brown tallied four catches (on four targets) for 53 yards in a preseason loss to Jacksonville on Saturday.
items.s: Brown tied for the Saints lead in receptions and finished second on the team in receiving yards behind Bub Means (77 yards). The highlight of Brown's performance was a 28-yard connection down the sideline with Zach Wilson late in the second quarter to help set up a field goal. Brown was taken by New Orleans in the sixth round of April's NFL Draft and had a chance to vie for a significant role among a Saints WR corps that lacks experience behind No. 1 option Chris Olave. New Orleans drafted both Jordyn Tyson (first round) and Bryce Lance (fourth round) ahead of Brown in the draft, but Tyson…

items.h: Brown has been among the Saints' top performers through seven training camp practices, Ross Jackson of Louisianasports.net reports.
items.s: Brown provided the highlight of Thursday's practice on a 46-yard touchdown catch from Spencer Rattler in a two-minute situation. The rookie sixth-round pick is building momentum in a Saints receiving corps led by Chris Olave and rookie first-round pick Jordyn Tyson. Brown will likely make his NFL debut Aug. 15 in the Saints' preseason opener against the Jaguars.

items.h: The Saints selected Brown in the sixth round of the 2026 NFL Draft, 190th overall.
items.s: Brown is a speedster who can take the top off the defense, compiling 53 catches for 532 yards and one touchdown in his senior season at LSU. He's very thin at 5-foot-11, 177 pounds, and he profiles as more of a sprinter than a polished route runner. Brown will likely be asked to add weight and muscle mass to his frame at the next level, and he'll need to clean up drops -- he totaled 21 drops over four seasons in college.
